$schema.what: THE EDGE REGISTER (s308-D16, Dave 2026-09-29 09:26 BST: '1. Write one edge register — Take it'). Every edge type in the knowledge graph, defined ONCE: one row per type actually present in the graph the explorer builds (knowledge/_build_kg_explorer.py extract() + extract_extra()). Read by knowledge/_validate_edges.py, which checks every edge against its row (s308-D17, advisory first) and checks that the register covers the graph (blocking).

fields.word: Apollo's storage type — the word on the edge. Never renamed here (s308-D22 keeps Apollo's words).
fields.plain: how the line reads, s → t, in plain words
fields.verb: which of the twelve verbs in knowledge/_kg_verbs.json reads this type, with its force (must / should / is); `unread` or `missing` where none does. Read from that file when this register was written.
fields.from: the node kinds (id prefix before the colon) an edge of this type may START from. CHECKED.
fields.to: the node kinds it may END at. CHECKED. An empty list means the type exists only as declared nulls.
fields.pairs: optional: where `from` × `to` would admit a wrong combination, the legal (from, to) pairs. CHECKED when present.
fields.nulls: whether a declared null (t: null, carried with its prose) is legal for this type, and the ruling or code that says so. CHECKED.
fields.opposite: s308-D18: the opposite relation (`type`: a word, 'itself' for a symmetric type, or null), whether THIS side is the stored one (`stored`), the rule that chose it (`basis`) and, for the pairs that were stored on both sides, the one-off agreement check run before the switch. A row with stored:false is READ by walking its opposite backwards; any edge of it still in storage is named by the check (READ-SIDE-STORED). CHECKED.
fields.reads: s308-D18: the two readings — `forward` s→t and `back` t←s. The explorer reads an incoming edge with `back` (its `read` block is built from this field), so the opposite is derived here, never stored as a second edge.
fields.shape: s308-D19: may it point at itself (`self`), may a chain of it return to its start (`loops`), does it hold both ways so it is stored once (`bothWays`), is it read transitively (`chains`); `basis` says why, `measured` what the graph holds. CHECKED: SELF-LINE, LOOP, BOTH-WAYS-STORED.
fields.count: how many targets one start may have (distinct targets). CHECKED where `perStart.max` is set, and set only where a definition says one; `basis` names it.
fields.why: s308-D20: the ONE name for an edge's reason is `why`. `required` says whether every edge of the type must carry one (true on the nine hand-made judgements s308-D20 names), `floor` its minimum length in characters (40 on obeys, kept), `servedBy` where another field serves (the ruling-to-ruling types' evidence), `today` how it is spelled and carried in storage. CHECKED by _validate_edges.py --check: WHY-MISSING, WHY-SHORT.
fields.maker: s308-D21: who made the type's edges, one of three — `hand` (by: whose/ruling), `generated` (by: which script) or `ratified` (by: which ruling); `none` only on a read-side row that stores nothing. `value` is the string every edge of the type carries as its `maker` (`<made>:<by>`), stamped by knowledge/_build_kg_explorer.py; `cases` override it by the edge's family (`fam`) or start kind (`from`); a stored line carrying its own `maker` keeps it. It replaces the `authored` flag, which is retired from the graph. CHECKED by _validate_edges.py --check: NO-MAKER, AUTHORED-FLAG.
fields.outside: candidate outside terms from lane O's v2 word map (Canonical ds:/dt:, Adobe Spectrum, then SKOS / Dublin Core / PROV / Kruchten / IBIS / ARIA). CANDIDATES ONLY: the choice and the grade are owed to item 7 (s308-D22).
fields.family: the explorer's storage family for the edge (fam), as built
fields.$measured: live tallies when this row was written; drift is reported by the check, never a failure

$schema.kinds: a node's kind is its id's prefix before the first colon (component:, rule:, ux:, …) — the grammar _validate_kg.py enforces.

$containers.what: THE CONTAINER MODEL (#309 lane B, enacting s308-D39..D44). 'Container' is this register's UMBRELLA WORD for anything that accepts children - a layout, a housing or a record - and never a component name, except the layout utility's width container (s308-D41). Every component meta declares ONE kind (meta `kind`; an alias seat is its owner's kind). A container's slots say which kinds they accept (`slots.<name>.accepts.kind`); a container with no kind-bearing slot accepts what its kind accepts below. knowledge/_validate_edges.py --check reads this block and every containedBy line (ACCEPTS, advisory first - s308-D40).

terms.card: one of a set of like records (s308-D39). A record; bounded by its border (surface: border). A lone card is a tile (s308-D43, warns).
terms.tile: one bento cell, surfaced, holding one thing (s308-D39). A housing; paints its own ground (surface: ground). No component is a tile today: the bento's tiles live only in template-dashboard-bento's markup, so `tiles` below is empty.
terms.cell: the grid position only - where something sits in a bento and what it spans; it has no surface and is not a part. A tile is the surfaced thing that occupies a cell (s308-D44).
terms.container: the umbrella word for a layout, a housing or a record - never a component name, except the layout utility's width container (s308-D41).
terms.surface: a PROPERTY, never a type: ground, border or none (s308-D41; meta `surface`).
terms.panel: a region of the screen frame only - a side panel, a drawer, a splitter pane (s308-D41). Not a content box; the role once called chart-panel is `chart` (knowledge/roles.json).

layout.plain: arranges several things (a bento, a card grid, a page template, a shell)

housing.plain: frames exactly one thing (or one sequence) with its own surface or behaviour - tile, carousel and panel are housings (s308-D44)

record.plain: one of a set of like records - a card (s308-D39)

block.plain: carries content, the thing the reader came for (a metric, a chart, a table, a list, an image)

part.plain: a named piece of one component (a card's header); a subcomponent: node is a part

limits.CARD-HOLDS: refuses (s308-D43 limit 1): a card never holds a layout, a housing or another record
limits.TOO-MANY: refuses (limit 2): a tile holds exactly one thing - a tile's accepting slot may not be multiple
limits.TILE-IN-TILE: refuses (limit 2): a tile never sits directly in a tile - nest through a bento
limits.MIXED-SLOTS: refuses (limit 3): a carousel's slides all hold the same kind - a sameKind slot may not accept two kinds
limits.LONE-CARD: WARNS (limit 4): a card always has peers - a record accepted by a housing through no multiple slot is a lone card, which is a tile
limits.NOT-ACCEPTED: refuses (s308-D40): the parent does not accept the child's kind
limits.MISSING: refuses (s308-D40): a required kind-bearing slot that accepts no containedBy line
limits.NO-KIND: refuses: a component meta with no kind (an alias seat excepted)
